_dispositions.ignored: Sleeper holds it and it genuinely does not apply — reason required
_dispositions.imported: something READS it — measured, not asserted. `evidence` names where.
_dispositions.imported_unread: it reaches league_config.json and NOTHING reads it there. Produced-and-unread (rule 14): the import is doing work no consumer collects.
_dispositions.should_import: Sleeper holds it, nothing reads it, and it matters — the `why` has to say what breaks without it

_hand_held._what: Facts Sleeper does NOT hold. These cannot be imported; the honest state is an explicit list with reasons rather than a vague sense that most things come from the API.
_hand_held.keeper_cost_model: Sleeper holds max_keepers:3 but NOT what a keeper costs (top_picks_flat: keeping N forfeits rounds 1..N)
_hand_held.my_draft_position: claimed by hand BY DESIGN; the war room verifies it against the draft object once the order is assigned
_hand_held.payout_split: house rule — reg-season and playoff percentages, in SEASONS
_hand_held.pre_2023_career_records: previous_league_id walks back only to 2023. Sleeper holds ~45 of 85 games per owner; the rest is structurally unavailable.
_hand_held.standings_tiebreaker: searched every settings key for tie/seed/rank/sort/standings — only playoff_seed_type exists. Points-for is a house rule, not an unread field.

_what: Every key Sleeper emits in league.settings, and what we do with it. A key Sleeper starts emitting that is NOT in here fails draft/tests/sleeper_registry.test.js — so a new setting gets CLASSIFIED rather than silently ignored, which is how waiver_type sat unread while the waiver system was held by memory. THE `imported` DISPOSITION IS MEASURED, NOT DECLARED. The first version of this file was hand-written from a reading of the import and claimed 19 imported; ten of those were read by nothing at all, and the test passed because it checked the key SET and the presence of a reason, never a consumer. It is now derived by two probes — draft/tools/settings_influence.py PERTURBS each setting and re-runs the import offline (path A: does it reach league_config), and draft/tools/settings_access.py looks for the shape of a read with comments stripped (path B: src/ reads Sleeper's settings straight off the season bundle, never through league_config). draft/tests/test_settings_registry_truth.py fails if this file and those probes disagree in either direction.

bench_lock.why: bench locks at kickoff; affects lineup-edit deadlines

daily_waivers.evidence: reaches league_config.waivers and nothing reads it
daily_waivers.why: 0 (off), which is why daily_waivers_days/_hour are ignored. Reaches config.waivers.daily_waivers; read by nobody.

daily_waivers_days.why: bitmask, only meaningful with daily waivers (off)

disable_adds.why: adds enabled; flag only matters when set

disable_trades.why: 0 — trades are ENABLED, the permissive state, so a gate on this flag would be a no-op today. It becomes should_import the day it flips, not before.

draft_rounds.why: 3 — AND IT IS WRONG FOR THE BOARD. The DRAFT object says settings.rounds = 15; the league setting is the pre-draft placeholder. config_schema.draft_rounds() exists because of this disagreement. Reading this key would build a three-round board, so ignoring it is the fix, not an oversight.

faab_suggestions.why: FAAB UI hint, and this league is not FAAB

league_average_match.why: no median-match game in this league

leg.why: 1 — which week of the season the league is on. Duplicate: the site takes the week from /v1/state/nfl (src/sleeper.js), which is right even when a league object is stale.

max_keepers.why: read ONLY by draft/backtest/exp_discoverability.py, which uses it to pick which PUBLIC leagues to sample — nothing that models OUR league reads it. Sleeper says 3 and sleeper_import hard-codes keepers.count=3 separately: two places for one fact, and Sleeper's is the authority.

num_teams.why: 10 — duplicate of league.total_rosters, which sleeper_import uses because it counts actual rosters rather than a declared target. Safe only while the two agree, so test_settings_registry_truth asserts they do.

pick_trading.why: draft-pick trading is ENABLED and nothing models it; it can move pick order before the draft

playoff_round_type.why: 0 = one week per playoff round, and money_grade's bracket resim plays round r in week playoff_week_start+(r-1), which is only correct for 0. It is now ASSERTED at the point that converts rounds to weeks: a league configured for two-week rounds is refused rather than graded, because every harvested bracket is round_type 0 and a two-week path would be certified by nothing. An absent value is refused too — a default that matches today is how the assumption goes invisible again.

playoff_seed_type.why: 0 — how the bracket seeds. The playoff cut is derived in several places and none of them consult it; it is also the only seeding-adjacent field Sleeper holds, which is why the tiebreaker sits in _hand_held.

playoff_teams.why: read by src/routes/* off the raw season bundle, NOT via league_config — sleeper_import also copies it into the config where nobody reads it.

playoff_type.why: bracket variant, covered by playoff_round_type for our purposes

playoff_week_start.why: read by src/routes/* and draft/backtest/money_grade.py off the raw season bundle. The config copy is unread; the season-bundle read is the real one, and it is 16, not the 15 the defaults assume.

reserve_slots.why: 1 — A ROSTER SPOT roster_slots_from() STRUCTURALLY CANNOT SEE. It counts roster_positions, which lists no IR entry, so the slot count is 15 and this capacity is invisible to it whatever its size. INFERRED, NOT MEASURED: that this makes the roster 16 rather than 15-with-one-IR-eligible follows from Sleeper holding IR outside roster_positions, and is not confirmed here — confirm by counting a roster's `players` against 15 once someone is on IR.

taxi_slots.why: 0 — no taxi squad, same as the rest of the taxi_* family.

trade_deadline.why: week 11, and no in-season surface knows it. A buy/sell recommendation made after week 11 is not an action anyone can take.

trade_review_days.why: 2 — a trade is not final for two days. Deadline arithmetic that treats an accepted trade as immediate is wrong by two days in the week that matters most.

type.why: league type (1 = keeper). Same single consumer as max_keepers: the public-league sampling filter, not our pipeline.

veto_auto_poll.why: whether a veto poll opens automatically

veto_show_votes.why: whether veto votes are public — affects vote mechanics

veto_votes_needed.why: trade veto threshold (5 of 10) — unmodelled in the trade/vote surfaces

waiver_bid_min.why: FAAB-only, and this league is not FAAB

waiver_budget.evidence: reaches league_config.waivers and nothing reads it
waiver_budget.why: 100, and meaningless: waiver_type is 1, so is_faab is correctly false. Reaches config.waivers.budget; read by nobody.

waiver_clear_days.evidence: reaches league_config.waivers and nothing reads it
waiver_clear_days.why: 2. Reaches config.waivers.clear_days and is read by nobody. Needed by any in-season claim-timing surface, which does not exist yet.

waiver_day_of_week.evidence: reaches league_config.waivers and nothing reads it
waiver_day_of_week.why: 2, and UNRESOLVED: the UI says waivers clear 2 AM WED, which matches 2 only if Sleeper counts Monday as 0. Nothing reads it, so nothing is wrong today — but it must not be read until the convention is confirmed against a real clear.

waiver_type.evidence: reaches league_config.waivers and nothing reads it
waiver_type.why: 1 = reverse standings, confirmed against the UI. valuation.js's waiverPriorityDepletes() turns exactly this code into depletes:false, but nothing wires the imported value into it — the rule and its input are both built and not connected.
